title: Deterministic dependency lockfile and CUDA driver prober for LTS promotions
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Add a deterministic dependency lockfile and a lightweight host-side CUDA driver prober to make image promotion to LTS channels safe and auditable. The lockfile will capture exact image digests, base layer references, SBOM pointers, and a validated driver ABI compatibility token. The prober binary (cuda-prober) will run in onboarding scripts and on Dedicated/Private hosts to report driver version, kernel ABI, and GPU feature flags; this report will be used by the promotion pipeline to cohort hosts and gate LTS rollouts. Goal: reduce runtime breakage during upgrades and enable safer automated promotions and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: CI generates dep.lock.json for every release build containing: image digest, base images with digests, SBOM URL, cosign signature reference, and driver-compat token
dep.lock.json is signed with cosign and stored in the artifact registry alongside the image
SBOMs are validated (SPDX 2.2 or CycloneDX 1.4) and linked from the lockfile
cuda-prober binary returns a canonical JSON payload with fields: driver_version, kernel_version, nvidia_uvm_present, cuda_abi_level, gpu_arch_list
Promotion pipeline rejects promotion if lockfile signature or SBOM validation fails
Rollout gate can target host cohorts by driver_compat token and allow staged canaries (5%, 25%, 100%)
E2E test harness can replay a dep.lock.json to reproduce the exact runtime image and driver pairing
Documentation and runbooks created: lockfile format spec, prober usage, promotion gating guide

risks: Hosts with older kernels may not expose expected ABI flags and could be incorrectly grouped
Lockfile format changes mid-release could make replay fragile
Cosign key management adds operational overhead and must be integrated with KMS/HSM
SBOM generation across multi-stage builds may miss transient build-time packages
mitigations: Prober will include a fallback probe that runs a small kernel module check and reports unknowns explicitly
Lockfile v1 will be stable; v2 requires explicit migration path and tooling to rewrite historical lockfiles
Use existing KMS-backed cosign key pair and rotate via runbook; automate re-signing in CI for emergency fixes
Add a build-stage SBOM diff job to detect omitted layers and surface false negatives before signing
rollout_plan: Phase 1: opt-in experiments on non-customer Dedicated clusters with 5 test hosts. Phase 2: cohort-based canaries (5% of hosts with matching driver token) for 48 hours. Phase 3: 25% for 72 hours with automatic metrics checks (latency error rate, OOMs, model mismatch). Phase 4: full promotion after 7 days of green telemetry. Abort conditions: >0.5% increase in 5xx errors or any critical kernel OOMs.
test_plan: Unit tests for lockfile generator, integration tests that perform lockfile replay on ephemeral infra, prober end-to-end tests on CI VM matrix (ubuntu 20.04/22.04, RHEL 8), and rollout simulation harness that replays historical telemetry to validate gate thresholds.
observability: Expose prober reports to internal telemetry (labels: host_id, driver_compat_token). Add dashboard: 'Driver-Image Cohorts' showing cohort health, promoted image digests, and SBOM validation status. Alerting: SBOM-signed-lockfile failure, signature mismatch, and cohort error-rate spike.
notes: This approach deliberately separates SBOM verification from driver compatibility checks so we can fast-fail on provenance issues without blocking longer-running host cohort discovery. Consider future: integrate with Optimize to suggest quantization profiles for driver cohorts. Coordinate with runtime team to map cuda_abi_level to kernel-module expectations.
